text: The Article disclaims the moral reading of its own slogan: rights follow stake is a boundary case about allocation, claiming no moral right for any intelligence system, with most of the framework being regulatory permission.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939

isBasedOn.name: Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights?

abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.

additionalProperty.name: supporting_quote
additionalProperty.value: "Rights follow stake" is the slogan, not the claim. The thesis is a boundary case. It claims no moral right for any intelligence system, and most of the framework is regulatory permission.
